 Anastasia Mason, Salem Statesman Journal Updated Tue, November 17, 2026 at 12:08 AM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Percent of Oregonians voting in 2026 midterms lags past elections A record breaking number of Oregonians voted in the 2026 midterms , though the percent of eligible voters who cast a ballot currently lags previous years.
 Unofficial ballot returns show more than 2 million ballots received across the state, accounting for 65.34% of the 3.1 million active Oregon voters.
 "Oregon once again had a safe, accurate, and fair vote-by-mail election. Despite unprecedented uncertainty over the past few months, we achieved our goal of a high turnout, low drama election," Secretary of State Tobias Read said. "Thank you to the record number of Oregonians who trusted us with their vote and to everyone who made this election possible."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement About 75.4% of Oregon voters cast a ballot in the 2024 presidential election, down from 82% in 2020.
 Oregon's average voter turnout in the midterms was about 70% between 2002 and 2022. The 2022 midterm was the lowest of those, with 66.9% of registered voters participating. Turnout for 2026 is currently below that, though it is the first midterm with more than 2 million Oregonians voting.
 Close to 1.5 million of those ballots were turned in before Election Day. Oregon accepts ballots received up to a week after the election as long as they were postmarked by Election Day.
 The Secretary of State's Office provided reports on voter turnout in the days leading up to the election, though no actual voting results were tabulated until 8 p.m. on Nov. 3. Results in Marion County were delayed after an envelope sorting machine broke on election night.
 Advertisement Advertisement Counties must certify their election results by Nov. 30. The Secretary of State's Office will certify the results by Dec. 10.
